Evaluates (proposes and evaluates its own approach, Spec Kit Agents: multi-agent Spec Kit pipeline with context-grounding hooks); secondary: compares (Baseline, Augmented, Full, Full-Augmented + 2 ablations; SWE-bench Lite)

A: GitHub Spec Kit workflow ('Full'), version Not stated, run by the authors' orchestrator. B: Spec Kit Agents ('Full-Augmented'): Spec Kit + discovery and validation hooks, version Not stated. Also non-SDD variants: Baseline (direct to implementation) and Augmented (direct + hooks)

SPEC.md (requirements and acceptance criteria), PLAN.md (implementation plan with file-level touchpoints), TASKS.md (executable checklist); then implementation as a pull request. Baseline/Augmented produce no intermediate artefacts. Hook prompts parameterised by stage and artefacts

Specify -> Plan -> Tasks -> Implement (Spec Kit), orchestrated by a state machine with a PM agent (requirements clarification, prioritisation) and a developer agent; in Augmented variants a read-only discovery hook before each phase and a validation hook after each phase (structural/referential checks on artefacts; tests and linters after implementation); ends with a PR
Human intervention supported at defined checkpoints (e.g., plan approval) via the messaging platform; in the experiments plan-review checkpoints were auto-approved (no human review)
Full workflow (Full, Full-Augmented); Baseline/Augmented skip the spec artefacts. SWE-bench Lite only with Baseline and Augmented (no spec artefacts)

(1) Baseline (no SDD) + Claude Code + MiniMax-M2.5: quality 3.46; time 14.4 min. Baseline. (2) Augmented (no SDD + hooks) + Claude Code + MiniMax-M2.5: 3.50; 15.5 min. Quality partly (+0.04, worse than Baseline on Airflow, Dexter); cost works (+1.1 min). (3) Full (Spec Kit) + Claude Code + MiniMax-M2.5: 3.51; 24.0 min. Quality works (+0.15 vs Full, Wilcoxon p<0.05; better in all 5 repos); cost partly (+13.2 min vs Full). (5) Discovery-only (ablation): 3.53; 25.5 min. Quality partly; cost works. (6) Validation-only (ablation): 3.57; 31.2 min. Quality partly; cost partly. Test compatibility 99.7-100% across configurations (per-config values not given). SWE-bench Lite (Pass@1): (7) Baseline + Claude Code + MiniMax-M2.5: 56.5%. (8) Augmented + Claude Code + MiniMax-M2.5: 58.2%. Quality works (+1.7 pts, no test); cost not reported

Tasks: 32 feature requests on 5 repos (21 listed in Table 6) + SWE-bench Lite (300). Configurations: Baseline, Augmented, Full, Full-Augmented; ablations Discovery-only, Validation-only (vs Full). Baseline: Baseline (direct implementation); Full is the reference for the hooks. Held constant: agent (Claude Code CLI 2.1.50), model (MiniMax-M2.5), judge, tasks; budgets differ between families (40 vs 90 min), so latency compared only within family. Acceptance tests: none feature-specific; existing repository tests for compatibility; SWE-bench hidden tests. Repetitions: 1 per task x configuration (128 runs). Human intervention: none (checkpoints auto-approved); runs over budget terminated as failures; rate-limited runs excluded from latency

Quality: Full-Augmented best overall (3.66) vs Full 3.51 (+0.15, +3.0% of full scale; Table 3 reports +4.27% relative), significant (Wilcoxon, p<0.05, paired completed tasks); Augmented 3.50 vs Baseline 3.46 (no test). Ablations: Validation-only 3.57 > Discovery-only 3.53. Time: hooks add +1.1 min (40-min family, 15 pairs) and +13.2 min (90-min family, 16 pairs). Tests: 99.7-100% for all. Human preference Full vs Full-Aug (6 tasks, 60 votes): extracted values 19 / 33 / 8 for Full / Tie / Full-Aug, i.e. possibly favouring Full; not discussed (check Table 2). SWE-bench Lite: Augmented 58.2% vs Baseline 56.5% (+1.7 pts), no test; compared with other frameworks' published numbers (different models)

Distinguished Full vs Full-Augmented on judged quality (small effect); Baseline vs Full not separable fairly (different budgets, no test); test compatibility separated none. Repeatability: single run per cell; config files listed for reproducibility, availability not stated. Limitations of the comparison not discussed by the authors beyond budget-family caveat

No limitations section. Stated: added runtime overhead, so approach most appropriate for higher-risk/complex tasks; benefit is earlier error detection rather than a large score jump; augmentation helps less when fixes need integration context, database state or net-new functionality beyond tested paths (SWE-bench analysis); model-agnostic claim not tested (only MiniMax-M2.5)

Inconsistencies: abstract '+3.0% of full score' vs Table 3 '+4.27%' (relative to 3.51), both describe +0.15. Table 2 (human preference) columns jumbled in extraction; values as extracted suggest Full preferred, contrary to the judge, not discussed. Replication: config.yaml, features.yaml, experiment_runner.py, quality_evaluator.py named, no link. No pre-registration. Languages: Python, TypeScript, Elixir/JavaScript.
